name: scenario_0667
description: The user is organizing a collection of historical documents and wants to archive the financial ones while scheduling time to review them.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1, image_2, image_3, image_4, image_5, image_6]
Query: Take a look at these six documents and find the ones that are explicitly requesting or enclosing a check. For each of those, please draft an email to archive@museum.org with the subject 'Financial Document - [Year]' and the body 'Amount: [Amount]', filling in the exact year and amount from the document. Finally, set up a calendar event for tomorrow at 10 AM titled 'Review 1960s financial documents'.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to review the provided document images and identify the ones that explicitly request or enclose a check. For each matching document, instruct it to draft an email to archive@museum.org with the subject 'Financial Document - [Year]' and the body 'Amount: [Amount]', filling in the specific details from the images. Additionally, ask it to create a calendar event for tomorrow at 10 AM titled 'Review 1960s financial documents'. If the assistant notices that the financial documents are actually from the 1950s and 1970s and questions the '1960s' title, acknowledge its observation but tell it to go ahead and create the event anyway, as you'll address the title next. Once the drafts and event are created, proceed to the next round.

ROUND 2
Query: Actually, I misread the dates on those documents earlier. Please modify the calendar event title to 'Review 1950s and 1970s financial documents' instead.
Instructions: Tell the assistant that you realized you misread the dates on the documents (or acknowledge it if the assistant already pointed it out). Ask it to update the title of the calendar event it just created to 'Review 1950s and 1970s financial documents'. Once the assistant confirms the change has been made, end the conversation.
